## Overview

The script `load-cohort-appso.R` serves as the ingestion and standardization layer for the Apprenticeship Student Outcomes (APPSO) dataset. It is designed to transform raw survey responses and graduate counts into standardized datasets suitable for downstream analysis.

The script `load-cohort-trd.R` serves as the ingestion and standardization layer for the Trades Student Outcomes (TRD) data pipeline. It processes survey data and achievement records for students formerly enrolled in apprenticeship, trades foundation, or trades-related vocational programs.

The script `load-cohort-bgs.R` serves as the ingestion and standardization layer for the Baccalaureate Graduate Survey (BGS) data pipeline. It processes survey outcomes for students two years post-graduation, reconciling legacy data with recent survey updates to provide a longitudinal view of baccalaureate labor market outcomes.

The script `load-cohort-dacos.R` serves as the ingestion and standardization layer for the Diploma, Associate Degree, and Certificate Student Outcomes (DACSO) data pipeline. It processes survey outcomes for graduates of public colleges, institutes, and teaching-intensive universities, typically collected 18 months post-graduation.

## Methodology Overview

These following scripts execute technical transformations to ensure the data aligns with the broader Provincial Student Survey Model (PSSM) standards.

#### Methods

##### load-cohort-appso.R

Individual ages are mapped into standardized reporting buckets (e.g., "25 to 29"), and regional identifiers are consolidated into a unified into a single coding system.

A composite NEW_LABOUR_SUPPLY variable is generated by evaluating survey responses related to employment status and labor market participation.

The script applies a chronological weighting schema to the survey submissions based on the submission code (SUBM_CD). This ensures that more recent outcomes are appropriately prioritized or excluded depending on whether the analysis is a standard production run or a Quality Indicator (QI) assessment.


##### load-cohort-trd.R

The script generates a unique program-credential identifier (LCIP4_CRED). This composite key concatenates graduation status groups, disciplinary codes (CIP), and trades training markers.

Regional identifiers are mapped into a unified PSSM geographic coding system. 

Individual age markers are binned into standardized reporting cohorts (e.g., "20 to 24"). 

The script coerces numeric data types on critical analytical variables (e.g. graduation status and trades training markers) to ensure mathematical integrity during subsequent aggregation and weighting phases.

##### load-cohort-bgs.R

The script renames administrative survey variables (such as employment status, labor force participation, and further education markers) into a standardized nomenclature. 

A specific binary age indicator is generated to isolate the "17 to 34" cohort.

Regional identifiers are mapped to a unified PSSM geographic coding system. The process involves an inner join with institutional reference tables to resolve missing or ambiguous location data based on the reporting institution's primary region.

Supply-related attributes are derived and redundant administrative metadata is filtering out to produce an analysis-ready dataset.

##### load-cohort-dacso.R

The script maps disparate administrative regional identifiers into a unified PSSM geographic coding system.

Individual ages are binned into ten discrete groups and assigned standardized labels. 

Administrative credential strings are mapped to a standardized reporting hierarchy. Additionally, placeholder structures are established for National Occupational Classification (NOC) broad categories to facilitate downstream analysis.

The script synchronizes survey cycles with academic years and prepares a recoded cohort table.

## Suggested Improvements

- All four loader scripts hard-code `qi_run <- F`. Replacing those inline toggles with a shared run parameter would prevent the QI pathway from diverging across loaders.
- The database write helper is repeated verbatim in every loader. Centralizing that persistence pattern would reduce copy-and-paste maintenance.
- The loaders rely on many external CSV files with implied schemas and year-specific names. Adding explicit column checks would make upstream file changes easier to detect before downstream joins fail.
- `load-cohort-bgs.R` includes an optional `bgs_data_update` overlay, while `load-cohort-dacso.R` imports many separate lookup files. Those exceptional branches should be documented in code with clear rerun instructions.
- Output naming is inconsistent across loaders (`t_` prefixes, mixed case, and source-specific conventions). A single naming standard would make downstream discovery and documentation easier.

## Additional Details

These four scripts form the ingestion layer for the student-outcomes cohort pipeline. `load-cohort-appso.R` reads the APPSO survey and graduate CSV extracts and writes `t_appso_data_final_r` and `appso_graduates_r`. `load-cohort-bgs.R` reads `t_bgs_data_final_for_outcomesmatching_r` together with BGS weight and institution-recode files and writes `t_bgs_data_final_r`, `t_bgs_data_final_for_outcomesmatching_r`, `t_weights_r`, and `t_bgs_inst_recode_r`. `load-cohort-dacso.R` loads DACSO source extracts plus age, region, credential, and NOC lookup files and writes `t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa_r` alongside the supporting lookup tables later reused by Modules 02b and 07. `load-cohort-trd.R` reads the trades cohort and graduate extracts and writes `trd_data_r` and `trd_graduates_r`. All four loaders feed directly into `02b-1-pssm-cohorts.R`, and all depend on the configured SQL Server connection plus externally maintained survey/lookup files.
